title: Create a Slack canvas with AI for a focused handover
h1: turn your handover notes into a new slack canvas
description: Create a titled Slack canvas from notes, optionally as a channel tab. See why channel placement grants write access and needs its own review instruction.
answer:
**give the next shift a handover they can find.** a bot turns your notes into a new slack canvas, with an optional title and channel tab. leave out the notes to start blank.

naming a channel adds a tab with write permissions. include content and placement in your review; creation doesn't wait for sending approval.

review.by: lead agent, after two independent reviewer passes, against Metal docs and the composio catalog

og_line: a new canvas for a specific handover.
what:
**put the handover beside the conversation.** naming a channel adds the new canvas as a tab there, with write permissions. leave the channel out to create it without that placement. ask for the canvas reference here; don't rely on a channel announcement.

title and content are optional: slack names an untitled canvas, and no content gives you a blank document. each run creates a fresh canvas rather than updating last week's.
uses: **hand over the next shift.** turn confirmed notes into one canvas people can find.
**prepare a workshop checklist.** give the facilitator the instructions you chose.
**keep the event run sheet nearby.** add its canvas as a writable tab in the named channel.
**start blank on purpose.** create a titled canvas for someone to fill during the session.

routine.message:
every other monday at 10:20, read the last fortnight's handover notes in #fenwick-shift. prepare a canvas titled fenwick night shift handover followed by today's date. use only instructions confirmed in those messages.

show the content and proposed #fenwick-shift channel tab here. ask me before you change anything. after i agree, create it and return its reference. never invent missing instructions or repeat an existing dated handover. create nothing when there are no new notes.
routine.needs: slack read and write for channel history, lookups and canvas creation; access to the destination channel
routine.output:
canvas proposal: fenwick night shift handover, 16 november

- ruxandra holds the gate checklist
- inspect the loading bay before locking up

destination: fenwick-shift channel tab, with write permissions
review the notes and channel placement together.

steps: **allow the needed slack actions.** connect with read and write for channel reads, lookup and canvas creation.
**choose content and placement.** give it a title. name a channel only when you want a tab there.
**ask for the proposal.** review the notes and destination before creating anything.
**open the first canvas.** find its tab and read the notes. pause the routine when the shift changes.
watch: **review before creation.** canvas writes follow your ask-first instruction, rather than sending approval.
**a named channel gets a writable tab.** include that placement in your review.
**missing notes mean an empty canvas.** missing title means slack chooses the name.
**each creation makes a fresh canvas.** it does not update an older handover.

faq.q: will a new canvas automatically become a channel tab?
faq.a: **only when you name a channel.** that placement adds it as a tab with write permissions.

faq.q: can i create just a blank canvas with a name?
faq.a: **yes.** give the title without content. say it should stay blank so the bot does not try to fill missing notes.

steps: ask for a canvas proposal, without creating it
choose whether it belongs in a channel
confirm the channel placement before allowing creation

mistakes.mistake: naming a channel as casual context
mistakes.fix: say whether you want a tab there. channel placement includes write permissions.

mistakes.mistake: creating a fresh copy of the same handover every fortnight
mistakes.fix: use new dated shift notes and skip handovers already saved.

items: the title names the shift and date
every instruction comes from a real handover note
the channel tab and its write access are intentional
this dated handover does not already exist

tip.text: a handover earns its place by telling the next shift what changed.
